package_info.why_malicious: EvilExtractor is a comprehensive attack tool designed to steal sensitive data, exfiltrate it to an attacker-controlled FTP server, and optionally deploy ransomware. It employs anti-analysis, anti-VM, and anti-sandbox techniques, and is distributed via phishing campaigns disguised as legitimate files. Its modules are explicitly designed for credential theft, keylogging, webcam capture, file exfiltration, and ransomware, with no legitimate use case.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks the system date and, if outside a hardcoded range, deletes PowerShell history and terminates execution, preventing analysis outside the campaign window.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware rarely restricts its execution to a specific date range unless attempting to evade analysis or limit exposure.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not self-delete logs or restrict execution based on arbitrary date ranges.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Time-limited trial software may restrict features after a date, but does not delete logs.

if product_model in ["VirtualBox", "VMWare", "Hyper-V", ...] or hostname in [list_of_187_scanner_hostnames]:

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks for virtualization or sandbox environments by matching product model and hostname against known analysis environments, terminating if detected.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Anti-VM and anti-sandbox checks are classic malware evasion techniques.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not terminate based on VM or sandbox detection.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some DRM or licensing systems may check for VMs, but not with such extensive lists.

malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not silently download and run credential-stealing modules.

attack_chain.action: Phishing email delivers a disguised executable (PyInstaller-packed Python or .NET loader) to the victim.

attack_chain.action: Malware checks system date and environment (anti-VM, anti-sandbox, anti-analysis).
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload execution only on real victim systems

attack_chain.action: Malware downloads and executes additional modules for browser data theft, keylogging, and webcam capture.
Malware collects files of interest, captures screenshots, and aggregates credentials.
Malware uploads all stolen data to an attacker-controlled FTP server.
Optionally, malware downloads and runs ransomware module to encrypt user files and display ransom note.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of PowerShell scripts with anti-VM and anti-sandbox checks
Bulk file collection from user directories (Desktop, Downloads) with sensitive extensions
Automated FTP uploads to external servers
On-demand download and execution of additional payloads (browser stealer, keylogger, ransomware)
Password-protected zipping of user files (ransomware behavior)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for suspicious PowerShell or Python processes that perform anti-VM checks, delete PowerShell history, or download and execute additional payloads from hardcoded IPs/domains. Flag bulk file access and copying from user directories, silent screenshot or webcam capture, and automated FTP uploads. Look for the presence of known payload files (KK2023.zip, Confirm.zip, MnMs.zip, zzyy.zip, 7za.exe) and ransom note files. Network monitoring should alert on connections to known malicious IPs/domains and unexpected FTP traffic.
